data.notes_riya: both are food but not same type of food; wendy's is a restaurant while the other packages food
data.notes_barbara:
Different products; Different customers; Different business model

B&G sells packaged grocery foods rather than restaurant meals. Food-related products alone do not make it a peer.
data.notes_matthew: B&G owns grocery brands like Green Giant and Crisco and sells through retailers and distributors. A packaged food company is not a restaurant comp.

data.reason: Wendy's runs and franchises quick-service hamburger restaurants. It sells prepared food directly to consumers through drive-thru, in-store and delivery orders. B&G Foods owns a portfolio of more than 50 packaged food brands, and the evidence shows it as an acquirer and brand owner of established food brands. Its customers are grocers, mass merchants and foodservice distributors, not diners. The two share only the broad food sector. They differ in product (restaurant meals vs. packaged goods), customer (consumers vs. retail and distributor accounts) and revenue model (restaurant sales and franchise royalties vs. wholesale product sales).

Different business model: B&G manages a portfolio of food brands for family food purchases; Wendy's offers made-to-order restaurant meals. General references to food and families do not establish a shared restaurant offering.
